worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}^{3}-{x}_{2})=3{x}_{1}^{2},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}^{3}-{x}_{2})=-1 \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{2}{e}^{{x}_{1}})={x}_{2}{e}^{{x}_{1}},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{2}{e}^{{x}_{1}})={e}^{{x}_{1}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}^{2} & -1 \\ {x}_{2}{e}^{{x}_{1}} & {e}^{{x}_{1}}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The linear approximation of $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
1+(-1)+1=1.
$$
html:
Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x1=∂∂x1(x13−x2)=3x12,∂f1∂x2=∂∂x2(x13−x2)=−1∂f2∂x1=∂∂x1(x2ex1)=x2ex1,∂f2∂x2=∂∂x2(x2ex1)=ex1

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[3x12−1x2ex1ex1].

Evaluating f and its derivative at x=a=[0−1], we have

f(a)=[1−1],f′(a)=[0−1−11].

The linear approximation of f at x=a is given by

f(x)≈f(a)+f′(a)(x−a).

Substituting f(a), f′(a), and a in the equation above, we obtain

f(x)≈[1−1]+[0−1−11](x−[0−1]).

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

1+(−1)+1=1.
